top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, mature and independently reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once, and JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE and NIST agree at the 10^-18 level, resolving gravitational redshift inside a single sample. It is separable from the frequency comb (2005) and single-ion control (2012) already honoured, and attribution to Katori (concept, first strontium lattice clock) and Ye (precision realisation) is clean with a two-laureate allocation. My reservation, that this is metrology and no new physics has yet emerged from the clocks, is a cost I accept rather than a reason to withhold the award, so no award ranks below it.
